title: Parents pay $75k for Alpha's AI school. Half of its students missed math target
lede: Fortune, citing internal data first reported by The New York Times, says only 42% of Alpha School students met its goal of learning twice as fast in both math and reading.

points: Alpha replaces teachers with guides and relies on TimeBack, its AI tutor app, for two hours of academics a day.
About half of K-8 students missed the math target; of those who started behind, only 37% met it.
Parents and guides told Wired that students worked late at night, which undercuts the two-hour premise.
Over 2,600 public school students in Texas and South Carolina now use the platform, including a Houston pilot.
Former staff told 404 Media the AI produced faulty lesson plans and that courses were scraped without permission.

points.text: Commenters split on the numbers: doubling the learning rate for 42% of students may be impressive rather than a failure.
One commenter argues the real claim is six times normal schooling, and that cutting learning time is the wrong goal.
The prizes Alpha pays students for results draw doubt about whether its outcomes are a fair benchmark.
A cited study, homework scores up and exam scores down after AI adoption, sparks debate on AI as aid versus crutch.
